MIT Breakthrough Technologies, 2001–2026

Every list MIT Technology Review has published of its "10 Breakthrough Technologies", from 2001 to 2026 (there was no 2002 list): 250 picks. For each one we mark what happened since, as our reading: mainstream, real but limited, or stalled. See which fields the editors bet on, how often they were right, and how AI took over the list.

Colour by:

Tap a technology

Each box is one pick. The purple outline marks AI picks. Tap for the field, what happened since (our reading) and MIT’s page.

How often the picks came true, by list year

Which fields the editors picked, by period

How to read it. The lists and technology names are MIT Technology Review’s. The field and the outcome for each pick are our reading as of November 2026, not MIT’s and not measured data: “mainstream” means in wide everyday or industrial use; “real but limited” means it exists and is used but stayed niche, slow or smaller than promised; “stalled” means it faded, failed or is still only in labs. Picks from 2024 on are marked too recent to judge. Names link to MIT’s pages (2021–2026 link to that year’s list).

Source: MIT Technology Review, 10 Breakthrough Technologies archive. Disclosure: Claude, made by Anthropic, helps write this site.
